title: Make a failed stock reservation explain itself

blocks.text: The checkout service reserves stock for each line of an order before it takes payment. On Black Friday the reservations started failing, and the alert channel filled with `ReservationFailedException` lines that nobody could act on: the on-call engineer couldn't tell which product had failed, or whether the stock database had rejected a lock, timed out or run out of connections. The checkout service itself only needs the SKU and the quantity, to tell the customer which line couldn't be reserved.

items: `reserve(...)`, which takes the stock from the store.

blocks.text: When you're done, a failed reservation tells the checkout service which line failed, and the log line and stack trace of the exception tell the on-call engineer the same, plus everything the database said. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: a reservation the store accepts takes the stock and throws nothing
a store failure reaches the caller as a ReservationFailedException whose getters name the SKU and quantity
the store's own exception, with its stack trace, is the cause of the reservation failure
the exception's log line names the SKU and the quantity

origin.section: Context Goes in Final Fields and in the Message

concepts: A wrapper keeps the original exception and its stack trace only if it is passed the cause, so the (message, cause) constructor is the one never to leave out.
Context goes in final fields for code and in the message for the log, because toString() and the stack trace show only the class name and the message.
